clue.text: Remove it perhaps to reduce earnings?

definitions.text: Remove it perhaps to reduce earnings?

parts.words: Remove it perhaps to reduce earnings?
parts.note: cutting the extra hours worked beyond the normal day is an obvious way for a pay packet to shrink

explanation.surface: Advice on trimming a wage bill by getting rid of something unnamed.
explanation.definitionFit: Hours worked beyond the standard shift are paid extra, so scrapping them lowers pay.

clue.text: Hence Chesterton's tea

parts.note: G. K. Chesterton wrote that tea, although from the East, is a gentleman at least; hence means the place it comes from

explanation.surface: A literary aside about where the writer Chesterton got his tea.
explanation.walkthrough: The allusion is to Chesterton's comic verse 'Tea, although an Oriental, / Is a gentleman at least'; the answer is where such tea comes from.
explanation.definitionFit: The East, the lands of Asia, is where Chesterton's tea came from.

clue.text: Skilful forward, once on top

indicators.note: in a down clue, 'on top' places the first piece above the second

parts.note: once means former, ex
pert, in an older sense, means bold or forward

explanation.surface: A football report praising a talented forward of the past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forward' looks like a footballer, but it means cheeky.
explanation.definitionFit: Skilful and masterly are synonyms for someone highly proficient.

clue.text: Try to contact Feathers

parts.note: to touch is to make contact
down is soft fine feathers

explanation.surface: An instruction to attempt getting in touch with someone called Feathers.
explanation.walkthrough: In rugby a try is scored by grounding the ball, also called a touchdown.
explanation.definitionFit: A rugby try and a touchdown both name the scoring grounding of the ball.

clue.text: Central place of' worship for' lawyers?

parts.note: central means middle
a temple is a building for worship

explanation.surface: A question about a central church used by members of the legal profession.
explanation.walkthrough: The Middle Temple is one of the four Inns of Court in London, the societies to which every English barrister belongs.
explanation.definitionFit: This Inn of Court is a society of barristers, so it stands, with a question mark, for a body of lawyers.

clue.text: Lithe and slim maybe, consuming in this way

indicators.note: consuming means one piece swallows the other, so it goes around it
maybe suggests the word slim could be some other arrangement of its letters

parts.note: so means in this way

explanation.surface: A description of someone supple and slender, perhaps because of how they eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' turns SLIM into LISM, and 'consuming' puts SO inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Lithe and supple are synonyms for a body that bends gracefully.

clue.text: Here French queen appeared more frigid

parts.note: ici is French for here
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for a queen

explanation.surface: A French queen arrived here looking colder than before.
explanation.definitionFit: Frigid means cold, so more frigid is colder, like ice.

clue.text: House-master's wife's' playful hand-out at tea-time

definitions.text: House-master's wife's' playful hand-out at tea-time

parts.words: House-master's wife's' playful hand-out at tea-time
parts.note: at a boarding school the housemaster's wife comforts homesick pupils over tea, so what she hands out is kind fellow feeling rather than food

explanation.surface: At a boarding school, the housemaster's wife hands round something at tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hand-out at tea-time' suggests buns or cake; what is handed out is comfort and fellow feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: Compassion and kindly understanding are what a caring housemother offers pupils.

clue.text: Fruit of invasion?

parts.note: the floating harbours built for the 1944 Normandy landings shared their code name with a soft dark berry

explanation.surface: A question about what some invasion produced.
explanation.walkthrough: The Allies' prefabricated D-Day harbours were code-named after a tree fruit, so the fruit belongs to the invasion.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a dark berry, and also the code name of the 1944 invasion harbours.

clue.text: Shuts up one member heading Jorrocks's pack

indicators.note: heading means the first pieces come at the front of the next

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
MP is a Member of Parliament
Jorrocks, the Cockney hunting grocer in R. S. Surtees's novels, drops his aitches, so his hounds are 'ounds

explanation.surface: Someone silences an MP who leads a fox-hunting character's pack of dogs.
explanation.walkthrough: John Jorrocks is a Cockney fox-hunting grocer in Surtees's comic novels; Cockneys drop the H, so hounds becomes OUNDS.
explanation.definitionFit: To impound is to shut up animals or goods in an enclosure.

clue.text: So miserable an actor of Dickens was Jemmy

definitions.text: an actor of Dickens was Jemmy
definitions.meaning: ... Jemmy is the gloomy strolling actor in Dickens's Pickwick Papers

explanation.surface: A remark that a gloomy Dickens actor named Jemmy was very miserable.
explanation.definitionFit: Gloomy and wretched cover the adjective; Dismal Jemmy is the melancholy player in Dickens's Pickwick Papers.

clue.text: Odorous course to rough descent

parts.note: sweet is the dessert course of a meal

indicators.note: rough suggests the word descent is roughed up into a new order

explanation.surface: A smelly track leading down a rugged slope.
explanation.definitionFit: Odorous means having a smell, fragrant.

clue.text: A point for the Prime Minister

definitions.meaning: one of the points of the compass
Lord ... was British Prime Minister from 1770 to 1782

explanation.surface: Something in favour of the head of government.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a compass point, and Lord North led Britain's government during the American War of Independence.

clue.text: Bring down a bag of letters

parts.note: to lower is to bring down
a case is a bag for carrying things

explanation.surface: An instruction to lift down a sack of post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letters' suggests mail but means small printed characters, named after the printer's lower tray of type.
explanation.definitionFit: Small type characters, as opposed to capitals, from the compositor's lower tray.

clue.text: Underling makes hay cleaner

parts.note: a bottle is an old word for a bundle of hay
a washer is something or someone that cleans

explanation.surface: A junior farmhand freshens up the hay.
explanation.walkthrough: A bottle of hay is a dialect term for a bundle; 'chief cook and bottle-washer' is a dogsbody.
explanation.definitionFit: A menial dogsbody doing the lowliest jobs, as in 'chief cook and bottle-washer'.

clue.text: Wandering in East Canberra possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals that these letters could form another word

explanation.surface: A stroll through the eastern part of Australia's capital, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Straying or deviating from the normal course, a departure from the norm.

clue.text: Whistler walked around when introduced

indicators.note: around means the walking piece goes round the official

parts.note: paced means walked
a referee, or ref, blows a whistle

explanation.surface: The painter Whistler strolled about when presented to people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whistler' suggests the painter, but it is a referee.
explanation.definitionFit: To preface something is to open it with an introduction.

clue.text: Trained to be dead cute, oddly

indicators.note: oddly suggests the letters of the two words are put in an odd order

explanation.surface: Someone schooled into being unbearably charming, strangely.
explanation.definitionFit: Schooled and instructed both describe someone who has been taught.

clue.text: He could have taught Cowper's linen-draper a thing or two

definitions.text: He could have taught Cowper's linen-draper a thing or two

parts.words: He could have taught Cowper's linen-draper a thing or two
parts.note: William Cowper's comic poem John Gilpin tells of a linen-draper hopelessly carried off by a runaway horse; an equestrian instructor could have helped

explanation.surface: Someone who could have given a lesson to the draper in Cowper's poem.
explanation.walkthrough: In William Cowper's ballad John Gilpin, the linen-draper cannot control his galloping horse; he needed horsemanship lessons.
explanation.definitionFit: An instructor in horsemanship teaches people to control a horse.

clue.text: Land in this car

definitions.meaning: a large area of owned property
a car with a long rear load space, called a station wagon in America

explanation.surface: Arriving at a property in a car.
explanation.definitionFit: A landed property is one sense; the other is a car with a rear load area, an American station wagon.

clue.text: Good report about Russian, it appears

parts.note: c, circa, means about
red is an old byword for a Russian communist

explanation.surface: A favourable account of a Russian, so it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: Credit is praise or good repute, a favourable account of someone.

clue.text: A milkmaid's dowry proved insufficient

parts.note: in the nursery rhyme the milkmaid says her face is her fortune, and the suitor declines to marry her

explanation.surface: A dairymaid's marriage settlement turned out to be too small.
explanation.walkthrough: The rhyme 'Where are you going to, my pretty maid?' ends 'My face is my fortune, sir' / 'Then I can't marry you'; her looks were her only dowry.
explanation.definitionFit: The worth of the milkmaid's looks, her only fortune, as opposed to real wealth; idiomatically, apparent worth.

clue.text: Shell part of valley about five

indicators.note: about means the valley word goes round the numeral

parts.note: a vale is a valley
V is the Roman numeral five

explanation.surface: A piece of shell from a valley about five miles off.
explanation.definitionFit: Each half of a bivalve mollusc's hinged shell is one of these.

clue.text: One responding to alarm in flight

definitions.meaning: someone who gets out of bed when the alarm clock rings
the upright part of each step in a flight of stairs

explanation.surface: Someone reacting to an alarm while airborne.
explanation.definitionFit: One who gets up from bed, and the vertical board of a stair step.

clue.text: Fish for the Captain

definitions.meaning: a cephalopod, loosely called a fish, as in cuttlefish
Captain ... is the kindly old sailor in Dickens's Dombey and Son

explanation.surface: Seafood ordered for the ship's captain.
explanation.definitionFit: The cuttlefish, and Captain Cuttle of Dickens's Dombey and Son.

clue.text: A sort of English rose-tree perhaps

definitions.meaning: the accepted form of the language is called ... English
a rose grafted onto a tall upright stem is called a ...

explanation.surface: Describing an English variety of rose bush.
explanation.definitionFit: Standard English is the norm form of the language; a standard rose is grown on a single tall stem.

clue.text: Twining plant appears to be decrepit

definitions.meaning: a leafless parasitic climber that twines round its host
to totter or move shakily with age

explanation.surface: A climbing plant looks past its best.
explanation.definitionFit: A parasitic climbing weed, and the verb to totter feebly with age.

clue.text: He stands by her during a depression

indicators.note: during means one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a dent is a depression in a surface

explanation.surface: A man stays loyal to his partner through a period of low spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'depression' suggests low mood but is a dent.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower or supporter is someone who sticks loyally to a cause.
